scope: Issue5046 exit: coherent public opt-in mode, short fixedS/Q capture, zero rotations, finite admitted retention, correct ownership/recovery and explained incremental costs; Store fences preserved.

actual_evidence.statistics: three descriptive repeats; no significance or production-tail claim

source_required_mechanisms: Private batch copies stabilize caller bytes through preparation; admitted C1 node copies preserve old immutable roots; next-cut/domain/vector allocations are ready before an accepted frame. Deleting admission/storage ownership or preparing after acceptance breaks the C2 lifetime/atomicity argument.

Existing canonical planner/finalizer is required by the accepted design. It verifies final key/value/revision and actual produced RID before visibility and independently pins live files/dictionaries. NoWAL already omits journal custody. Omitting canonical validation or dependent read pins is unsafe; changing to a new typed entry API is a separate authority design, not an established redundant deletion.

Both legacy and COW pointer Set encode before ACK. Registered COW publication also flushes producer visibility before actual-RID lookup and live read-pin installation. Ordinary legacy NoWAL Set may ACK buffered frames, flushing later through its read barrier. These end-to-end ratios therefore include publication/buffering/visibility differences; identical physical frames and exact incremental flush shares are unproved. Flush is not fsync.

COW pointer materialization owns finite admitted private codec/input/output buffers, validates CRC/length/window and copies output before release. The existing shared native-reader contract requires output scratch. Direct-output or borrowed-value consolidation could reduce a copy with a new verified ownership contract; deleting the shared copy today would invalidate callback/iterator lifetimes.

FixedS/Q cut capture retains existing roots and backend/resource owners without a history census. General forward iteration still requires cursor/merge ownership. The new successor uses existing lower bounds across all captured sources only for a proven-empty retained backend; physical tombstones/nonempty bases/missing capability retain the same-snapshot merge fallback.
